land.text: the Khmer realm of 1431 as Cliopatria draws it, with the court moving from Angkor to the Phnom Penh area

predecessors.note: The Khmer Empire dossier is drawn through 1431. The Post-Angkor page puts the Siamese intervention at Angkor 'around the year 1431' and quotes Briggs that the Cambodians 'reconquered their capital the next year', so Angkor stays in the realm.

land.text: Cambodia under King Norodom, a French protectorate from 11 August 1863; the monarchy stays in place

successors.note: Infobox 'French Cambodia: 11 August 1863'. Cliopatria keeps its Khmer shape to 1867 and draws Cambodia inside French Indochina only from 1868, so 1864-1867 are a gap (see notes).

capitals.name: Chaktomuk (Phnom Penh)
capitals.note: Infobox: 'Chaktomuk (1431-1525)'; Basan/Srei Santhor were also used by Preah Ram I and II ('moved the capital several times'), undated. The Khmer Empire page lists Chaktomuk with Angkor for Barom Reachea II (1405-1431).

capitals.name: Longvek
capitals.note: Infobox: 'Longvek (1525-1594)'; the page gives no year for Ang Chan I's move beyond the infobox. 'In 1594, Longvek was successfully captured and sacked by Siamese forces.' The Khmer Empire page says Barom Reachea I briefly returned the court to Angkor in 1566-1576; the Post-Angkor page is silent on that, so the capital is not moved here.

capitals.name: Srey Sarchor (Srei Santhor)
capitals.note: Infobox: 'Srey Sarchor (1594-1620)'. Coordinates approximate (Srei Santhor, Kampong Cham). 'In 1596 Spanish and Portuguese conquistadores from Manila raided and razed Srei Santhor.'

capitals.name: Oudong
capitals.note: Infobox: 'Oudong (1620-1863)'; the French protectorate page gives 'Oudong (1863-1866); Phnom Penh (1866-1953)'.

keyframe_review.note: 240,474 km2 for the kingdom that moved to the Phnom Penh area in 1431: Tonlé Sap, Angkor and the Mekong lands, plus the Mekong delta (140 of its 146 cells). The Post-Angkor page gives no area (only population: 1,224,000 in 1500). Years for this dossier: 1432-1474 (the Khmer Empire dossier takes 1375-1431).

correction.text: the 1475 shape without Bình Thuận, for 1475-1539

No page opened has Cambodia taking Cham land in 1475; the Nam tiến page has 'Champa's demise' in 1471 with the seizure of Vijaya and the annexation of what remained only in 1832, so the Cham south (Bình Thuận, 27 of the cells) is removed. The highland cells are kept, unverified: page budget.

keyframe_review.note: 274,386 km2: the same Cham/highland extras as 1475 (119 cells beyond the 1375 outline); no event on the pages opened changes the frontier in 1540. Bình Thuận removed as for 1475; unverified: page budget for the highlands.

correction.text: the 1579 shape without Bình Thuận, for 1579-1587

keyframe_review.note: 274,330 km2, the 1540 outline again (2 cells fewer); nothing on the pages opened for 1579. Bình Thuận removed; unverified: page budget.

keyframe_review.note: 274,386 km2, the same outline through the Siamese sack of Longvek (1594), which was a capture of the capital and not a change of border (the page: 'In 1594, Longvek was successfully captured and sacked by Siamese forces'). Bình Thuận removed; unverified: page budget.

correction.text: the 1653 shape without Bình Thuận, for 1653-1690

keyframe_review.note: 274,472 km2, the same outline while the Vietnamese first intervened militarily in 1658-59 ('The first Vietnamese military intervention took place in 1658-59', no land transfer on the page). The Mekong delta is still drawn Cambodian; the ledger shows it contested from 1658. Bình Thuận removed; unverified: page budget.

minus.text: Bình Thuận, the Cham south (Panduranga) that stays Cham to 1832

correction.text: the 1691 shape without Bình Thuận, for 1691-1699

keyframe_review.note: 273,733 km2; the page says 'by the end of the 17th century, the region was under full Vietnamese administrative control', so the Mekong delta in this shape is on its way out (lost in 1700). Bình Thuận removed; unverified: page budget.

184,854 km2: the kingdom without the Mekong delta, which fell under 'full Vietnamese administrative control' by the end of the 17th century. The 295 cells lost (141 delta cells plus the eastern extras) are almost exactly Cliopatria's separate 'Cambodia' row (1700-1802, 85,545 km2), which the Cambodia dossier reviews. No infobox area.
184,657 km2, an unchanged outline for 1702-1756; the pages opened give no frontier event in these years. Unverified: page budget.

184,771 km2 for 1757-1795 (one cell more than 1702). The page is silent on 1757 (Trà Vinh, Sóc Trăng, Hà Tiên), which belongs to the delta already lost. Dated 1757-1794: Siam annexes Battambang and Siem Reap in 1795.

114,867 km2: the north-west is gone (234 of the 237 cells lost lie in Cliopatria's Rattanakosin shape of 1796). Infobox 'Rattanakosin conquest of Siem Reap and Battambang: 1795'; text 'Siam annexed Cambodia's Battambang and Siem Reap provinces'. Dated from 1795 instead of 1796.

115,124 km2 (two cells more than 1796) for 1803-1858. The Vietnamese occupation of 1834-1847 ('Nguyen rule: 1834-1847', Tây Thành province) is drawn as a hatched occupation from the ledger, not as a change of shape.
114,896 km2 for 1859-1865. 'On 11 August 1863, Norodom signed a treaty acknowledging a French protectorate over his kingdom', so the independent kingdom is drawn through 1863 only.

correction.text: the same outline, for 1864-1867, as a French protectorate (tint of french-indochina) instead of an independent Cambodia

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria still draws Cambodia as the 'Khmer Empire' in 1864-1867 (this shape and the tail of khmer-empire_1859) and as French Indochina only from 1868. After 11 August 1863 Cambodia is a French protectorate in which 'the Cambodian monarchy was allowed to remain', so for 1864-1867 the same outline should be drawn as French protectorate land (the lighter tint of french-indochina), not as an independent state. Siam's 1867 renunciation is not dated on the page.

region.text: the Khmer lands that remained to the court at Chaktomuk (Phnom Penh): the Tonlé Sap basin, Angkor and the Mekong lands to the delta

ledger.note: 1432: after the Siamese intervention at Angkor, King Ponhea Yat holds the Khmer lands from the Phnom Penh area. Infobox 'Siege of Angkor: 1431'; the text puts the Siamese intervention at Angkor 'around the year 1431' and a citation of Briggs has the Cambodians 'reconquered their capital the next year'. The Khmer Empire dossier is drawn through 1431; the move to Phnom Penh (Chaktomuk) is from the Khmer Empire page.
1525: Ang Chan I moves the capital from Phnom Penh to Longvek (infobox 'Longvek (1525-1594)'; the text gives no year).

1594: the Siamese capture and sack Longvek ('In 1594, Longvek was successfully captured and sacked by Siamese forces') and the court moves to Srey Sarchor (Srei Santhor), infobox 'Srey Sarchor (1594-1620)'.
1620: the capital moves to Oudong (infobox 'Oudong (1620-1863)'). In 1618 Chey Chettha II 'stopped sending tribute to Ayutthaya and reasserted Cambodian independence'.

region.text: the Mekong delta, a 'hitherto Khmer domain'

ledger.note: 1658: the Vietnamese intervene in Cambodia for the first time. 'The first Vietnamese military intervention took place in 1658-59'; by 1620 the Vietnamese 'had reached the Mekong Delta, a hitherto Khmer domain' and about 1623 Chey Chettha allowed Vietnam a custom-post at Prey Nokor (Saigon). The page does not say the intervention moved a border; the contest over the delta is my reading.

region.text: the Mekong delta, a 'hitherto Khmer domain'

ledger.note: 1699: the delta passes under Vietnamese administration. 'By the end of the 17th century, the region was under full Vietnamese administrative control.' The page gives no treaty or last battle; 1699 is the year before Cliopatria's shape drops the delta.

region.text: the Mekong delta and the south-eastern lands: the 1691 shape without the 1700 shape (141 delta cells and the eastern extras)

ledger.note: 1700: the Mekong delta is lost to the Nguyễn lords. 'By the end of the 17th century, the region was under full Vietnamese administrative control' (the Nam tiến page dates nothing: 'wrested the southernmost territory from Cambodia by diplomacy and by force', undated). Cliopatria draws the lost cells as its own 'Cambodia' row (1700-1802); see notes.

region.text: Battambang and Siem Reap provinces and the north-western lands that Siam annexed

ledger.note: 1795: Siam annexes Battambang and Siem Reap. Infobox 'Rattanakosin conquest of Siem Reap and Battambang: 1795'; text 'Siam annexed Cambodia's Battambang and Siem Reap provinces'. The lost north-west is 237 cells of the 1757 shape.

region.text: Cambodia, organised by the Nguyễn as Tây Thành province

ledger.note: 1834: Vietnam rules Cambodia directly. Infobox 'Nguyen rule: 1834-1847'; 'Later that year, the Tây Thành Province was established' and a rebellion followed 'from 1840 to 1841'. Recorded by the owner, with the roles reversed. The page also says 'Cambodia fell to the Vietnamese invasion in 1811' without a land change.
1847: Nguyen rule ends (infobox 'Nguyen rule: 1834-1847'); the page then has Cambodia 'placed under joint suzerainty between the two regional empires' (Siam and Vietnam), undated.

region.text: Cambodia as a whole, a French protectorate from 11 August 1863

ledger.note: 1863: Cambodia becomes a French protectorate. 'On 11 August 1863, Norodom signed a treaty acknowledging a French protectorate over his kingdom'; 'the Cambodian monarchy was allowed to remain' with power 'largely vested in a resident general'. Infobox 'French Cambodia: 11 August 1863' (Post-Angkor period page). Siam recognised the protectorate later (undated on the page).

wars.name: Siamese capture of Longvek
wars.outcome: Longvek was captured and sacked by Siamese forces in 1594 and the court moved to Srey Sarchor; no border change is recorded on the page.
wars.note: The page adds that in 1596 Spanish and Portuguese adventurers from Manila raided and razed Srei Santhor, and that in 1618 Chey Chettha II stopped paying tribute to Ayutthaya.

wars.name: Vietnamese settlement and intervention in the Mekong delta

zones.text: the Mekong delta, a 'hitherto Khmer domain'

wars.outcome: Vietnamese settlers reached the delta by 1620, a custom-post followed at Prey Nokor (Saigon) about 1623, the first military intervention came in 1658-59, and by the end of the 17th century the delta was under full Vietnamese administrative control.
wars.note: The ledger starts the contest in 1658, the first dated military step; the page does not call the whole period a war.

wars.name: Siamese annexation of Battambang and Siem Reap
wars.outcome: Siam annexed Battambang and Siem Reap in 1795.

wars.name: Vietnamese occupation of Cambodia (Tây Thành)

zones.text: Cambodia, ruled as Tây Thành province

wars.outcome: Nguyen rule from 1834 to 1847 with a rebellion in 1840-1841; Cambodia then stood under joint Siamese-Vietnamese suzerainty.
wars.note: The page's 'fell to the Vietnamese invasion in 1811' is not followed by any dated land change.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey fixes any frontier on the pages opened; the Mekong delta, the north-west and the Cham/highland edge are approximate. The frontier with Siam after 1795 and the 1863 protectorate limits are not described on the pages.

notes:
Cliopatria row split. This dossier is the post-Angkor half (1432-1863) of the 'Khmer Empire' row (800-1867); the Angkor half is khmer-empire. The orchestrator asked for the split (800..1867 in one row). Wikipedia treats them as two articles ('Khmer Empire' 802-1431, 'Post-Angkor period' with the infobox successor 'Post-Angkor Cambodia'); the capital moved from Angkor to the Phnom Penh area, and the shapes after 1431 are a different, smaller realm. New slug: post-angkor-cambodia.

Overlap with other rows (decisions for the orchestrator): (1) Cliopatria's 'Cambodia' row (slug cambodia, 1700-1802, Wikidata Q424, Wikipedia title 'Cambodia Middle Period') is almost exactly the Mekong delta that the 'Khmer Empire' shape loses in 1700 (287 of 295 lost cells). The Cambodia Middle Period article is the Post-Angkor period article, so the 'cambodia' dossier (se-01-h) and this one describe the same kingdom, and its shape is the delta part. Either cambodia is written as the delta land (a Cambodian claim or a mislabelled Nguyễn lands) or merged here as a second Cliopatria name. This dossier does not claim the delta after 1700: the ledger records the loss to nguyen-lords (conf 2) and the contest from 1658. (2) kingdom-of-cambodia (1956-2024, also Q424) is a later state. (3) French Indochina's Cliopatria shape (1860-1867, Cochinchina) has no Cambodia until 1868, so 1864-1867 has no owner in Cliopatria except the Khmer shape; the khmer-empire_1866 verdict asks for it to be drawn as a French protectorate tint; the french-indochina dossier (se-03) should carry the 1863 protectorate as a vassal_start with counterpart post-angkor-cambodia.

Pages: nine opened for the whole row (see the khmer-empire dossier); here Post-Angkor period, Nam tiến (thin: it dates nothing about the delta), French protectorate of Cambodia. The page budget is spent, so the 1702 shape, the 1475-1699 highland extras and the 1803 shape are 'unverified: page budget'. The infobox gives no area; population only (1,224,000 in 1500; 1,419,000 in 1600; 1,650,000 in 1700; 2,090,000 in 1800).

Corrections: start 1432 (infobox 'Siege of Angkor: 1431'), the 1475-1699 shapes lose Bình Thuận (Cliopatria's Cambodia carries 160 cells of the Champa 1429 shape from 1475, 119 from 1540; the highland cells Lâm Đồng, Đắk Lắk, Đắk Nông, Bình Phước are kept unverified), the north-west goes in 1795, the independent kingdom ends 11 August 1863 and 1864-1867 should be a protectorate tint.

Left out: tribute to Ayutthaya (to 1618: 'In 1618, King Chey Chettha II stopped sending tribute to Ayutthaya') and to the Nguyễn (after 1658-59), and the Siamese-Vietnamese joint suzerainty after 1847: a vassal tint belongs in the suzerain's dossier (ayutthaya-kingdom, nguyen-lords, nguyen-dynasty, rattanakosin-kingdom) with counterpart post-angkor-cambodia; none is dated well enough on the pages opened. The Khmer Empire page says Barom Reachea I returned the court to Angkor in 1566-1576; the Post-Angkor page lists only Longvek for 1525-1594 and is silent on Angkor; the capitals follow the infobox. The 1811 'fell to the Vietnamese invasion' sentence and the 1840-41 rebellion are not drawn. Mekong delta dates: 1620 Vietnamese reach it, c. 1623 Prey Nokor custom-post, 1658-59 first military intervention, end of the 17th century full control; nothing dated for 1698, 1708, 1714 or 1757 on the pages opened (the Nam tiến page is silent on them too). Rulers omitted (no list was read).

Gazetteer names used: 'Mekong Delta' (region), 'Bình Thuận', 'Angkor (region)' is not used here. Coordinates of Srei Santhor are approximate.
